text.p: Here are highlights of stories reported by Hungary's press, based on information by Nepszabadsag's Hungary Around the Clock service. For further details on how to subscribe to Hungary Around the Clock, please contact Monica Kovacs at (361) 351 2440 or fax your request to (361) 351 7141.
ALL PAPERS
- President Arpad Goncz and Ukrainian President Leonid Kuchma inaugurated two new lanes of the Tisza bridge on the Hungarian-Ukrainian border on Friday. (Sat.) @
- Left-wingers within the Socialist Party Saturday blasted the party and its coalition partner as being "unable to live up to their election pledges".
- Eyewitnesses almost caught the man who threw a hand grenade outside a Budapest nightclub on Saturday. No injuries were reported.
MAGYAR HIRLAP @

- Some Socialist politicians reportedly raised the possibility of a December or January cabinet shuffle at last Monday's meeting of the party's presidential board. Meanwhile, the party presidential board is to meet this afternoon with the Free Democrat executive body.
- An extremely heated debate erupted during Saturday's meeting of the Free Democrats national council, with several politicians arguing in favour of quitting the coalition.
- Prime Minister Gyula Horn Friday inaugurated a House of Slovak Culture in Bekescsaba. (Sat.) @

-Jacques Roger-Machart, director of development at Electricite de France said his company "will try to exert diplomatic pressure on the Horn government so that cost-based energy prices be established, which also contain a profit rate.
- Ibusz Rt. announced after-tax profits of HUF 112 million on sales of HUF 3.72 billion in the first three quarters of the year.
MAGYAR NEMZET
- Parliament is set to start a debate on a bill on the state news agency MTI, but will devote most of its session to debating details of the 1997 budget this week. (Sat.) @
- Ferenc Vegh, Armed Forces Chief of Staff said on Friday that a nine-month military service for draftees would be introduced from November 1997 at the earliest. (Sat.)
- In summing up his Moscow visit, Speaker of Parliament Zoltan Gal said he found emphaty and understanding regarding the return of Hungarian art treasures taken to Russia in World War II. (Sat.)
- US President Bill Clinton awarded the Legion of Merit to retired general Bela Biro, former deputy commander of the Hungarian Armed Forces, and former head of Hungary's IFOR operations. @
VILAGGAZDASAG
- The Netherlands is extending HUF 500 million in support to Hungary in 1997 for more rational energy exploitation, environmental protection, agriculture and vocational training.
- Household net savings totalled HUF 46.7 billion in October, HUF 17 billion more than a year earlier.
- The EBRD is optimistic about Hungary's prospects for further development, despite its estimates that Hungary's GDP growth will be only 1.5 percent this year. @
- The Hungarian Oil and Gas Co. MOL recorded a pre-tax profit of HUF 1 billion on sales of HUF 104.5 billion in the first three quarters.
- OTP Bank recorded an after-tax profit of HUF 7.4 billion through the first three quarters of 1996.
NAPI GAZDASAG
- The gas supplier Primagaz closed the first nine months with an after-tax profit of just over HUF 1 billion.
- The Zalaegerszeg-based freezing company Goldsun laid off 120 of its 320 employees on Friday. (Sat.)
